title: Deciding bounded nondeterministic acceptance
statement: For every effective coding scheme $c$ for nondeterministic two-work-tape machines over the binary alphabet, there exists a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine $B$ such that, for every binary code string $\alpha$, there is a natural-number constant $C$ with the following property. For every binary input $x$ and every natural number $t$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ accepts $x$ along some choice string of length exactly $t$, then $B$ computes output $[1]$ on the paired encoding of the binary representation of $t$, $\alpha$, and $x$ in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not accept in this sense, then $B$ computes output $[0]$ on that same input in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: effective coding scheme $c$ for nondeterministic two-work-tape binary machines
replaced:
For every effective coding scheme for nondeterministic two-work-tape binary machines,
there exists a finite binary Turing machine $B$. For each code string $\alpha$, there is
a constant $C$ such that for every binary input $x$ and natural number $t$, if the
machine decoded from $\alpha$ has an accepting computation on $x$ within exactly $t$
choice steps, then $B$ computes the output $[1]$ on the paired encoding of the binary
representation of $t$, $\alpha$, and $x$ within $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it has no such
accepting computation, then $B$ computes $[0]$ on that encoding within the same bound.
